scope: Still-held sub-3000 candidates only; excludes resolved 2539/2715/2826/2987, Agent A new-lesson selection above 4000, and Pilot 3000–4000 triage

findings.sourceExample: Few new songs leave the same deep footprint for me.
findings.sourceMeaning: Have an equally lasting emotional impact; a footprint metaphor.
findings.ownerMeaning: Make a stronger lasting impression or influence, using a deeper-mark image.
findings.reason: The source compares the lasting emotional impact of songs using the same footprint image. Owner 398 teaches stronger lasting influence with deeper; add a bounded same deep footprint branch and comparison example before aliasing.

findings.sourceExample: The lyrics feel close to home for many listeners.
findings.sourceMeaning: Personally or locally familiar; a conventional home metaphor.
findings.ownerMeaning: Feel particularly relevant, affecting or uncomfortable because of a connection with personal experience.
findings.reason: Feel close to home has the same personal-relevance sense as owner 1079 hit close to home, but uses a different verb; teach both feel/hit frames and local-versus-personal context before aliasing.

findings.expression: the weight of a whole nation on their shoulders
findings.sourceExample: No artist should carry the weight of a whole nation on their shoulders.
findings.sourceMeaning: The excessive burden of representing everyone; a physical weight metaphor.
findings.ownerTitle: carry the weight of the world on their shoulders
findings.ownerMeaning: Feel burdened by overwhelming responsibilities or worries.
findings.reason: Carry the weight of a whole nation on their shoulders has the same overwhelming-representative-burden image as owner 59 weight of the world, but the noun slot changes; bound it to whole nation and teach the representation nuance before aliasing.

findings.sourceExample: Today, the spotlight is shared with online creators.
findings.sourceMeaning: Public attention is divided among figures; a stage-light metaphor.
findings.ownerTitle: the spotlight is not always equally shared
findings.ownerMeaning: Public attention is not distributed evenly on every occasion.
findings.reason: The affirmative spotlight is shared divides public attention, matching owner 1478 unequal spotlight distribution in the opposite polarity. A reviewed positive branch and assessment are needed before aliasing.

findings.sourceExample: Investigators were working in the dark until the records arrived.
findings.sourceMeaning: Operating without information or guidance; a fixed light metaphor.
findings.ownerMeaning: Remain partly uninformed or unclear about a situation.
findings.reason: Work in the dark means actively operating without records, while owner 163 teaches someone being left somewhat uninformed. Shared ignorance image is insufficient until the agentive work in the dark frame is deliberately taught.

findings.sourceExample: We have one free evening, so let's make the most of it.
findings.sourceMeaning: Use an opportunity fully; a conventional phrase.
findings.ownerTitle: make the most of limited space
findings.ownerMeaning: Use the available small amount of room as effectively as possible for the intended purposes.
findings.recommendation: retain hold pending broader owner decision
findings.reason: Make the most of one free evening is conventional opportunity use; owner 1616 is expressly limited to physical space. It needs a broad transferable owner rewrite or a separate learner decision, not a detector-only alias.

findings.sourceExample: Old songs remain part of the city's cultural memory.
findings.sourceMeaning: Shared remembrance within a community; a natural abstract collocation.
findings.ownerTitle: uncover a layer of cultural memory
findings.ownerMeaning: Discover an aspect of a community’s remembered past, using an image of revealing a hidden layer.
findings.reason: Cultural memory alone names shared remembrance; owner 406 teaches the specific action uncover a layer of cultural memory. Generic noun membership is not the same teachable construction.
